transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

I guess what brought me in is that I’ve kind of swung from barely being able to settle into my new apartment to suddenly taking on a lot. Like, I started saying yes to mentoring sessions, extra client prototype work, and then I decided I needed to redesign my whole portfolio all at once.

It felt like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint, and it’s been a lot.
Have you noticed any periods where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or you felt more energetic than usual, even if it didn’t last very long?

Yes. Earlier this month I had this stretch where I felt almost electric—really upbeat and charged up. But then I’d flip really quickly and get irritated, like snapping at a contractor or my sister over small delays. In the moment it felt like they were getting in my way on purpose, even though looking back it was probably minor.
Can you tell me how long that upbeat, charged-up feeling lasted? Was it a few days, a week, or longer?
It’s been about a month overall, since I moved into the apartment. The really intense up-and-down feeling has kind of been there through that whole period, not just one day.
Can you describe a time when you felt different from your usual self—like your mood or energy level was so high or irritable that it clearly stood out from how you typically feel?

Yeah, earlier this month was the clearest example. I felt almost electric, like really upbeat and wired, and then I’d switch pretty fast into being irritated. I remember snapping at a contractor and also at my sister over tiny delays, like in my head it felt like they were personally trying to block me. Looking back, that’s not really how I usually react.
Can you tell me if there was a specific time when your mood was so high or irritable that it was clearly different from your usual self—and if so, how long did that last?

Yes—earlier this month. I felt really different from my usual self, like almost electric and upbeat, and then I’d suddenly get really irritable. I snapped at a contractor and at my sister over small delays, like they were personally trying to block me. That stood out to me.
Can you tell me if the time when you felt that upbeat, electric mood—along with the irritability—lasted for four days in a row or more?
Yes, it was definitely more than four days. The intense up-and-down feeling has basically been going on since I moved into the apartment, so about a month now.
Can you tell me if there was a time when your mood was so upbeat or irritable that it lasted for a week or more without letting up?
Yes. I mean, it hasn’t really let up since I moved into the apartment—so about a month now. It’s been this intense up-and-down mood the whole time.
Can you tell me if your mood—whether it was upbeat, electric, or irritable—was present most of the day, nearly every day, during this time?

Yes, it was there a lot of the day. I’d feel almost electric and really upbeat, and then I’d flip into being irritated over small things. Like with the contractor or my sister—tiny delays felt like they were getting in my way on purpose. It felt pretty constant during that stretch.
During that time when your mood was so upbeat or irritable, did you also notice that you needed less sleep, your thoughts were racing, or you were more easily distracted than usual?

Yes, the sleep part definitely happened. For several nights I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours, but I’d wake up feeling like I was totally fine, like I didn’t need more sleep. I’d think I should just use the extra time to get ahead on things.

During that time when you felt so upbeat or irritable, did you find yourself doing a lot more things than usual—like taking on many projects at once, moving around more, or feeling like you had to keep going without rest?

Yes. I was doing way more than usual. I had barely even settled into my new apartment, and then suddenly I was saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and deciding I needed to redesign my whole portfolio. It felt like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint.
